contents.entry: The checks, one row each, with exit code and message shape
Mechanism: a suite row, a pod, check.sh
How it starts without an agent typing
Every wait, its timeout and its fallback
What this volume needs from the shared volumes

pointers.sibling: Input and output record schema of this node
Status code map loader, which depends on this gate refusing a bad map
Cleanup registry, whose generated registry this check verifies
Drive publish, which runs only after a merge this check passed
pointers.shared: The script this node runs (written by the shared author)
Retry layers: the spec-check unit retries nothing of its own
The spec-book unit is an ordinary suite pod

purpose.is: Makes the spec book's rules a gate: a pull request that touches rebuild/design cannot merge unless every volume passes XSD, every pointer resolves, no volume is over 1000 lines, every volume opens with a contents element, carries a parent pointer and a many agents at once section, and the generated files (index.xml, shared/record-kinds.xml, shared/cleanup-registry.json) match their source and dag.md agrees with itself (#checks).
Its verdict reaches the merge as part of coq/gate on the head sha (D05, N-25), so the agent can read it and cannot edit it.
purpose.is-not: It is not the review seat (N-19) and it is not the no-cog review of brief C; those judge meaning, this checks shape and references.
purpose.why: Owner order: the book is validated as a set, one XSD family, a check that every pointer resolves and no volume exceeds 1000 lines (memory spec-book-many-small-xml). The plan's own validator (rebuild/bin/plan-validate.sh) shows the pattern: XSD, then the checks XSD 1.0 cannot express, exit 1 on any error, exit 2 when the validator could not be set up.

input.record: A suite plan entry for a head sha whose diff touches rebuild/design/** (suites.json row paths rebuild/design/* maps to suite spec-book; the always row lint runs too).

output.record: Every check passed for the head sha; rows per volume with line counts; the generated-file hashes.
At least one check failed; one row per failure with volume path, check id, line and message; nothing else changes.

The checker could not run (exit 2: a validator or tool missing from the pinned image); a result like any exit code (nodes/N-24/spec.xml#m-ladder), never retried, because the image is pinned by digest and a retry runs the same image.
output.example: {"id":"20261015T062000Z-422-k9l0m","at":"2026-10-15T06:20:00Z","seq":4150,"epoch":1,"kind":"check.verdict","code":422,"node":"N-46","by":"N-24","body":{"head_sha":"89abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef","pr":57,"exit":1,"checks_run":["C01","C02","C03","C26","C28"],"failures":[{"volume":"rebuild/design/shared/ci-capacity.xml","check":"C26","message":"quota requests.cpu 4500m is not container-cap x suite + canary = 6700m"}],"log_path":"$COQ_STATE/ci/logs/gate/2026/10/89abcdef0123-1/units/spec-book.log","seconds":11.2}}
output.reads: N-25 (folds the verdict into coq/gate with the gate page link), N-19 (the reviewer brief carries the rows), N-47 (publishes only a merge whose main sha has a 201).

checks.s: The table below is the checker's own list, in the same ids as rebuild/design/bin/check-book.py prints (gap review R-03, 2026-10-14: the round 1 table named nineteen checks the script did not run, in other ids); a check is added by one ticket that declares this volume, check-book.py and a mutation in bin/test-checks.py (runbook step 3).
checks.check: Every .xml under rebuild/design parses.
Every volume validates against schema/volume.xsd (python xmlschema, or xmllint in the checker image).
Every volume is 1000 lines or fewer.
The first child of every volume root is contents, and every entry ref names an id of the same file, in document order.
pointers holds a parent pointer (href, or path plus anchor) that resolves.

Every pointer resolves to a file and, with a fragment, to an id (XML), a heading slug or line range (Markdown) or a JSON pointer (JSON); paths outside the repository and citations on another branch are notes, not failures.
A many-agents section exists and is not empty.
No em dash or en dash in any .xml, .md, .json, .sh or script of the book.
No id repeats inside one document.
Every *.schema.json is valid JSON Schema 2020-12 and every $ref resolves.
Every nodes/N-xx directory is a node of index.xml and the reverse, dag.md names the same set, every volume-ref resolves and its lines attribute equals the file's line count.
@node equals the directory name; @issued or @written is present.
Every wait names a timeout and a fallback; a wait whose timeout is none carries class level-triggered or owner-decision; class, when present, is bounded, level-triggered or owner-decision.

bin/registry.py --check: shared/cleanup-registry.json is generated fresh from every state-paths element and validates against its schema; every path names a cleanup; a host or external path with no script declares retention never and acts owner; a tracked or client path declares retention never.
bin/make-kinds.py --check: shared/record-kinds.xml is generated fresh from every node's status-codes section and every row parses.
bin/dag-check.py: the Mermaid block, the node and group tables, the re-entry table and section 6 of dag.md agree; every edge names a node; the graph is acyclic; the stated topological order is valid.
bin/make-index.py --check: index.xml equals the generated one (nodes, volumes, kinds, line counts).
Every kind of the registry is named by an emitter row of every code it carries in shared/status-codes.xml, and every code it carries exists there.
Every node-spec volume has an element with id input and an element with id output.
Every panel kind of the screen volumes and of N-37's index is a record kind (shared/record-kinds.xml), a view (nodes/N-31/spec.xml#views) or a static kind (nodes/N-37/spec.xml#static-kinds).

A pointer into a Markdown file never uses a list label (V04, T02, K07) as its anchor, in an attribute or in prose, and a Markdown pointer (path, hash, anchor) written in prose resolves like any pointer (R-03 review note: G4 volumes cited 02-MAPPING list labels as if they were anchors).

Every JSON example validates against the schema it names: an <example schema="file.json#/pointer"> in a volume, and each json block of DESIGN.md against the record.schema.json link above it; schemas resolve through their $id, so a $ref between nodes that does not line up fails too (bin/check-examples.py; R-03 round 4: the envelope example failed N-02 and N-01, N-02 and N-07 required different envelopes).
checks.s: Judged by the review seat, not by the script: the no-cog and many-agents reading of each volume, the brief's source list cited or rejected (shared/rejected-with-reason.xml), Mermaid that renders (the checker image's mermaid CLI runs it in the pod as a lint row of its own).
checks.exit: 0 all pass; 1 any check failed (one line per failure: FAIL check volume detail); 2 the checker could not run (no XSD validator). Every exit is a result of the unit (N-24: a command that ran is never retried): 0 is pass 201, 1 is fail 422, 2 is fail 422 with check.verdict 503, a defect of the pinned checker image.

mechanism.where: rebuild/design/check.sh in the repository, run as one pod case by N-24 from a suite.plan row (D22: tests and lint run as pods). The suites.json row is paths rebuild/design/*, suites spec-book; an unmapped path plans the full set, so a missed row never skips the check (V06).
mechanism.step: N-23 plans suite spec-book for the head sha; N-24 starts the pod from the pinned checker image (xmllint, python3 with xmlschema and jsonschema, the mermaid CLI, git), which fetches the repository by sha anonymously (public repo, A02).
The pod runs rebuild/design/check.sh; it runs C01 to C22 (#checks), never stopping at the first failure, and prints one line per failure and a final summary line with counts.

N-24 writes pod.run with the exit code and the log at N-24's host path ($COQ_STATE/ci/logs/gate/YYYY/MM/<sha12>-<attempt>/units/spec-book.log, nodes/N-24/spec.xml#state-paths); N-25 maps exit 0 to coq/gate success and exit 1 or 2 to failure for that case; the pod writes its check.verdict line to records/spec-book.jsonl and N-24's artifact import puts it in the store for this node (nodes/N-24/spec.xml#m-mirror; the spec-book suite entry lists check.verdict in its records, nodes/N-23/spec.xml#output).
On the host, the same script runs in make lint (always row) for the fast feedback a worker gets before pushing; the pod result is the verdict, the host run is advice.
mechanism.generated-files: index.xml (bin/make-index.py), shared/record-kinds.xml (bin/make-kinds.py) and shared/cleanup-registry.json (bin/registry.py) are generated; dag.md is checked by bin/dag-check.py; a ticket that changes a source regenerates and commits them in the same PR; the check refuses drift (C14, C15, C16, C17), so a hand edit to a generated file cannot merge.

diagram.mermaid: flowchart LR P[pr.opened head sha] --> N23[N-23 suite planner] N23 -- row rebuild/design/* --> N24[N-24 pod: check.sh] N24 -- exit 0/1/2 --> V[check.verdict 201 / 422 / 503] V --> N25[N-25 coq/gate on head sha] N25 --> N08[N-08 gate verdict]

start.s: A push to a PR branch is seen by the poll (N-04), planned (N-23) and run (N-24); nobody asks for the check and nobody can skip it, because coq/gate is a required status on main (D05).
The review seat of brief C runs the no-cog and many-agents judgement; this node runs the mechanical shape check first, so the review seat never reads a volume that fails C01 to C22.

wait.what: pod scheduling in the factory namespace
wait.fallback: N-24's pod-ladder (5 rungs) then one more plan attempt (shared/retry-budget.xml#layers); then pod.run infra and coq/gate error, which the agent reads as not green

wait.timeout: the unit's budget_minutes from the plan (floor 5, suite.budget), inside the pod deadline d-pod
wait.fallback: the timeout is a result, pod.run timeout 422, never retried; a run near its budget on a book under 100 volumes is a checker defect and becomes a fix ticket request

wait.timeout: PT0S at run time: the tools are in the pinned image or the run is exit 2 at once
wait.fallback: the image pins every tool by digest (images.json); check.sh never installs anything; a missing tool is exit 2

waits.cog-test: The cog that could stall this node is a human reading 50 volumes for shape. The script reads them in seconds and the forge refuses the merge without it.

retries.policy: This node retries nothing; only a pod that never ran check.sh climbs N-24's pod-ladder and then the plan-attempt layer; exit 0, 1 and 2 are results (V05; NF-E3: book 1.0.0 retried exit 2 three times against N-24's five rungs).
retries.recover: After the ladder and the last plan attempt, coq/gate carries error for the case; an exit 2 is check.verdict 503 and a failure on coq/gate; the next push re-plans.
retries.report: A 422 is not a card: the worker's next attempt (N-11) gets the rows in its brief; three failed attempts on one ticket follow N-11's dead path.

many-agents.readers: Every author reads this volume to know the rules; the rows in a 422 are addressed to the volume path, so seven group authors can read one verdict and each fix only their rows.
many-agents.writers: The check writes nothing in the repository; its check.verdict reaches the store through N-24's artifact import under the operation key of the import (head sha, unit, plan attempt, line), so two pods for two PRs never collide and a replay of the same import returns the first record (idempotent).
many-agents.collision: Seven authors pushing seven PRs that each touch index.xml or dag.md: the one-file, one-in-flight-ticket rule (N-14) refuses the overlap, so generated aggregates are regenerated by one ticket at a time; the group authors' node directories never overlap.

A volume that points at a sibling in another group's PR not yet merged: C06 fails on the head sha, which is correct; the author points at the index entry instead (the index carries every node id from the DAG even before its volume exists, with status pending), and the sibling pointer is added by the later PR.
Two spec-author seats on the same node (a retry after a failed verdict): N-14 refuses the second workspace; the retry starts after the first seat's seat.result.

status-codes.emits: Failed rows; seat acts on the next attempt (the worker or spec-author fixes).
Checker could not run (exit 2); a result, never retried; the image is fixed by a ticket (N-22) and coq/gate is a failure for the case.

state-paths.path: Output of make lint host runs of check.sh.
state-paths.rule: Pods write nothing on the host; the unit log is N-24's path and cleanup (nodes/N-24/spec.xml#state-paths), so this node registers no second path for it.

item.check: check.sh passes on the merged book at main.
item.proof: Exit 0 on main's head sha in a pod, pod.run log saved.

item.check: Each check C01 to C22 has a failing fixture.
item.proof: rebuild/design/bin/test-checks.py copies the book to a temporary directory, applies one mutation per check (a fixture made at run time, so no broken volume is ever committed and none goes stale), runs the checker on the copy and asserts that check fails; exit 0 when every check is proven, one line per check that did not fire.

item.check: A volume of 1001 lines is refused.
item.proof: Fixture C03; exit 1; row names the file and 1001.
Fixture C06; row names the href.
test-checks.py mutations C14, C15 and C17 (a stale registry, kinds file and index) and C16 (a dag.md table row with no Mermaid node); exit 1 each.
factory/config/suites.json has a row with paths rebuild/design/* and suite spec-book; N-23 test plans it from a diff touching nodes/N-43/spec.xml.

item.check: A missing tool is exit 2, a result that is never retried.
item.proof: A pod run with the image's xmllint removed: one pod, no rung, pod.run fail 422 exit 2, check.verdict 503 (not-run).

may.do: plan, run, write check.verdict, post the gate status
run check.sh on the host for advice; read verdict rows in its brief

may-not.do: write check.verdict; edit generated files by hand; edit the XSD and a volume in one ticket unless both are declared
nothing to refuse; the owner can override a merge only through the forge's own admin path, which is break glass and recorded by N-42

monitoring.counter: Which C-row fails most; the top row is a candidate for an author-side lint hint.
Count and the largest line count; an alert record when the largest passes 900 (split before it fails).
Run time; over 120 s is an alert.

runbook.step: Read the rows; fix the named volume lines; push; the check re-runs on the new sha.
The pinned checker image lacks a tool: a ticket fixes the image (N-22) and the plan's next head runs it; a coq/gate error with no 503 is the pod infrastructure and the N-24 runbook applies.
Add the C-row here, the fixture, and the row in check.sh in one ticket; the ticket declares rebuild/design/check.sh and this volume.
make lint runs check.sh; its output is under N-46.host-run.
runbook.cleanup: line/bin/cleanup.sh --entry N-46.host-run; the pod log is N-24's (ci/bin/cleanup-ci-state.sh --what gate-logs).

sources.source: check.sh validates the set: XSD, pointers, 1000 lines, contents, parent, many agents
XSD then semantic checks; exit 0, 1, 2; validator in a venv outside the repo
xmllint absent on the host on 2026-10-14; the pod image pins it
The Mermaid block and tables are generated; dag-check.py
Rows map paths to suites; always lint; unmapped means full
Data-driven planner, pod per case, digest pins, status on sha
V05 assertions never retried, V06 planner from the diff
The verdict the agent reads and cannot edit

source.anchor: Shape to apply in R-03 Design

sources.source: The book is validated as a set
A reviewer rejects a shape with no answer for the collision
The SPEC-16 per-domain checker: the pattern of a spec family with its own check script

reject.reason: A second XML format with its own checker for a v2.0 export that is 114 commits stale (04-UNLANDED.md section 2); the book has one XSD family and one checker.

reject.source: lint/lint.sh as the only runner of the check
reject.reason: The host lint aborted 54 times (L10 section 5.1) and is advice; the verdict must come from the pod and land on the sha.

reject.source: a human reading for pointer resolution
reject.reason: The owner's rule: the system drives; a reader is a cog.
Seven authors fix seven groups from one verdict; the check reports every row.

shared-needs.need: rebuild/design/check.sh running bin/check-book.py (C01 to C22) with the exit contract; bin/registry.py, bin/make-kinds.py, bin/dag-check.py and bin/make-index.py as its helpers (make-index.py --check is the index check); bin/test-checks.py as the fixture proof.

One XSD per volume kind in rebuild/design/schema/, with the kind attribute on the root; the elements this group uses: contents, pointers (parent, sibling, shared), purpose, input, output, mechanism, start, waits, retries, many-agents (readers, writers, collision), status-codes (emits), state-paths (path), edges (in, out), checklist (item, check, proof), permissions (may, may-not), monitoring (counter, lamp), runbook (step, cleanup, cold-start), sources (source), rejected (reject), shared-needs (need), effects, registry, safety, checks, diagram with mermaid CDATA.
A checker image in images.json with xmllint, python3 xmlschema and jsonschema, mermaid CLI and git, digest pinned.
factory/config/suites.json row paths rebuild/design/* suite spec-book; command rebuild/design/check.sh.
index.xml carries every DAG node id with status pending until its volume lands, so a sibling pointer to the index always resolves.
